summary:
A health monitoring web app for astronauts on Moon and Mars missions which shows each crew member their health in seconds and proves that the data behind it is real. Tracks heart rate, blood oxygen, blood pressure, body temperature, breathing rate and radiation dose, marks each with a color and a shape (normal, watch, act now), computes the NEWS2 early warning score.
Health decisions are made on board from sensor data, so a faulty or spoofed sensor, or a quietly edited record, can lead to the wrong care. Pulse & Proof signs every reading, chains every record, encrypts medical notes and gives each role only what it needs. Is possible to run it offline, models Moon and Mars signal delays and solar conjunction blackouts, and uses live NASA DONKI space weather and NASA-STD-3001 radiation limits. In a built-in simulation lab, all 13 attacks from our threat model were caught or contained, the slowest in under 10 seconds.
details:
The project is a crew health monitor for long missions where Earth can't answer in time. Each astronaut, the crew medical officer and the flight surgeon on Earth see the same health picture, each limited to what their role needs:

Six signs per person: heart rate, blood oxygen, systolic blood pressure, body temperature, breathing rate and radiation dose rate.

Color coding with shapes, so status is readable without color: green circle for normal, amber triangle for watch, red square for act now. Ranges follow NEWS2 and the AHA blood pressure categories.

The NEWS2 early warning score for each person, with the recommended response.

Live trend charts with shaded normal, watch and act-now bands.

Simple instructions: a ? on every card explains what the value means, why it matters in space and what to do.

Gamification: daily health tasks with points, levels, streaks and badges. Mood check-ins are stored encrypted.

Radiation: career dose against the NASA-STD-3001 limit of 600 mSv, background measured on Mars (Curiosity RAD) or the Moon (Chang’e 4), and live solar particle events and flares from NASA DONKI.

Moon and Mars modes with real one-way signal delays (1.3 s and 12 minutes), solar conjunction blackouts, and a store-and-forward link to Earth.

A signed health report that anyone can verify, and a simulation lab that runs mission events and 13 attacks and times how fast each one is caught.

It's a static web app that is possible to install and run offline, each simulated wearable signs its readings with its own Ed25519 key, and every reading carries a sequence number. The hub rejects unsigned, forged or replayed readings and flags values that freeze or jump. Every event is written to a SHA-256 hash-chained ledger, so any later edit breaks the chain and can be restored from the copy kept on Earth. Medical notes are encrypted with AES-256-GCM under keys unlocked by each person’s PIN (PBKDF2, 150 000 rounds), with lockout after 5 wrong PINs. Data to Earth travels in signed, encrypted bundles; commands from Earth must carry the flight surgeon’s signature. Every attack in the lab maps to a MITRE ATT&CK technique.

In the lab, 8 attacks were stopped instantly, attacks on the Earth link were caught as soon as the data arrived (one signal delay), an edited record was found in 1.4 s, and a sensor frozen at a normal value was flagged in 9.7 s. A long test run of 412 signed readings produced no false alerts.

The crew gets a view of their health and plain next steps. The medical officer and the flight surgeon can trust that each number came from a real sensor and was not changed. The system keeps working, and keeps warning, with no link to Earth.

Vital signs are simulated, because there is no public live stream of astronaut vital signs; authorized users can enter real measurements by hand. This is a prototype, not a medical device.
